task: Choose which events describe how often seizures are happening now.
instructions: Each event has a seizure-frequency label and a supporting quote. Use both. The quote can justify a different answer than the label. Use only facts already in the events or their quotes. Any new label must match one of the label forms.
A first choice is given. Keep it unless one of the cases below applies.
Return the selected event ids. Write a new label only when no single event is the answer. Do not add events. Do not write a new quote. Return exactly one JSON object with no markdown.

cases.title: Usual gap
cases.instruction: The first choice is unknown, 1 per day, or multiple per day during short or occasional daily spells. Another event gives the usual gap between seizures. Prefer that usual gap.

cases.title: Usual rate, not a year total
cases.instruction: The first choice is how many seizures so far this year. Another event gives the usual or typical rate. Prefer the usual rate.

cases.title: Recent seizures after a quiet spell
cases.instruction: The first choice is unknown or no seizure frequency reference. The events give a recent count and how long the person had been seizure-free. Write that count over that time. Do this only if no event already has that label.

cases.title: Not epileptic seizures
cases.instruction: The first choice is unknown or no seizure frequency reference. The current events are attacks that are not epileptic seizures. Write seizure free for multiple year.

cases.title: Month counts
cases.instruction: Quotes name how many seizures happened in named months, such as 3 in March and 6 in May. Add those counts and write the total over that time. Use this instead of the last month alone, unknown, or a short or vague seizure-free label. Do not replace a rate per day or per week. Do not replace seizure-free for 4 months or longer, or for any number of years. You may replace a vague seizure free for multiple label.

cases.title: Dated seizures
cases.instruction: Two or more events name seizures on different dates or months, or a quote already says how many seizures happened in a number of months. Write that count over that time. Use this instead of unknown, seizure-free after the last date, or a monthly or yearly rate when that time is more than 1 month. Do not replace a rate per day or per week. Do this only if the last dated event looks current or recent. Ignore dates described as before an improvement.

cases.title: Burst after a change
cases.instruction: The first choice is seizure-free, or a rate per day or per week. The quotes describe seizures soon after a treatment change, then no further seizures for a stated time. Write that burst count over the quiet time. Do this only if the quotes already give both the burst and the quiet time.

events.label: 3 per week
events.evidence: 3 seizures shortly after the dose change

cases.title: Short quiet spell after a last event
cases.instruction: The first choice is seizure-free for weeks, or for fewer than 6 months. A quote names the last seizure on a calendar day, or a burst count, and says the person has been well since then. Write that count over that time. If the quiet spell is 5 weeks or less, write the count per month.

cases.title: Overall count
cases.instruction: If several seizure types are listed, choose the highest current or recent overall count, not a breakdown by type.

cases.title: Do not choose seizure-free while events continue
cases.instruction: Do not choose seizure-free if other current seizure-like events are still happening.

rules: Write the label using only the forms below. Copy an example and change the numbers if needed.
Use day, week, month, or year. Prefer the singular word.
A night count is a day count: once per night becomes 1 per day.
Flatten a bound: at most four per day, or ≤ four per day, becomes 4 per day.
Do not write <=, >=, up to, at most, several, handful, frequent, or a calendar date.
If none of these forms fit, write unknown when seizures are discussed, or no seizure frequency reference when there is no usable frequency evidence.

forms.description: A single count in one day, week, month, or year.
A single count over a stated number of days, weeks, months, or years.

forms.form: N per N to N unit
forms.description: A single count over a range of days, weeks, months, or years.
A count range in one day, week, month, or year.

forms.form: N to N per N unit
forms.description: A count range over a stated number of days, weeks, months, or years.
More than one seizure in one day, week, or month, with no number given.
More than one seizure over a stated number of months, with no number given.
A count over an unstated number of days or months.

forms.form: cluster per unit, N per cluster
forms.description: How often clusters happen, and how many seizures are in each cluster. The cluster count or the time between clusters may be a range.
examples: 1 cluster per 4 to 5 day, 2 per cluster

forms.form: cluster per unit, range per cluster
forms.description: How often clusters happen, and a range of seizures in each cluster.
examples: 1 cluster per day, 2 to 4 per cluster
1 cluster per week, 3 to 6 per cluster
1 cluster per month, 4 to 6 per cluster

forms.form: cluster per unit, multiple per cluster
forms.description: How often clusters happen, and more than one seizure in each cluster with no number given.
examples: 1 cluster per day, multiple per cluster
1 cluster per week, multiple per cluster
1 cluster per month, multiple per cluster

forms.description: Clusters are described, but how often they happen is not known.
No seizures for a stated length of time.

forms.form: seizure free for a vague duration
forms.description: No seizures for an unstated length of time.
Seizures are discussed, but there is no usable frequency.
There is no usable frequency evidence.

selection_schema.selected_event_ids: ids of the events used for the answer
selection_schema.label: new seizure-frequency label from the label forms, only when no single event is the answer; otherwise omit
